correctness.rationale: The published Theorem 14 supplies the run-length identity. Exact integer matrix arithmetic proves \(M^{10}=I+4B\); the inverse recurrence gives \(s_{-6}=s_{-1}=0\), and the two integral first-order coefficients are 1 and 9. For every positive \(r\), the matrix quotient \( ((I+4B)^r-I)/(4r)\) is congruent to \(B\) modulo two in \(\mathbb Z_2\), since \(2(j-1)-\nu_2(j)\ge1\) for all \(j\ge2\). The two exact valuations therefore equal \(2+\nu_2(r)\), and run-length multiplicativity adds valuations for the stated binary-word class. Finite tests verify transcription, not the infinitely quantified theorem.

value.rationale: The congruence class of run lengths 4 modulo 5 is a complete natural arithmetic stratum of the studied run-length transform, not an arbitrary finite sample. The sharp unbounded valuation formula describes all Mersenne inputs in two infinite progressions and lifts to arbitrary binary words with such runs. It is a structural 2-adic invariant motivating further full-profile analysis, rather than a restatement of the pre-existing recurrence or a routine finite computation.
